description: A facilities operations director must decide whether to authorize a temporary exhaust fan for a solvent-cleaning cell and finalize the installation and operating controls, with input from maintenance and environmental health and safety.

shared_context.S1: The solvent-cleaning cell is scheduled to resume work on Monday morning.
shared_context.S2: A mobile exhaust fan is available in the plant and can be positioned at the cell's temporary duct connection.
shared_context.S3: The cell's existing exhaust has been adequate for its normal cleaning work, but the temporary fan would provide additional capture during the planned solvent-cleaning campaign.
shared_context.S4: Mara makes the final authorization, and the plant's Monday-start routine requires maintenance and environmental health and safety to review the setup before the decision is recorded.

PF1.text: Jon's electrical check found that the mobile fan must be connected to a dedicated 32-amp breaker because its startup draw can overload the cell's existing circuit; installing that breaker and the interlock will take exactly 2 hours, and he has not entered the check in the work-order system because the panel inspection was completed during the weekend shift.

PF2.text: Priya's air-monitoring review found a peak VOC reading of exactly 85 ppm at the cell during door-open cleaning, above the 50 ppm action level; the fan must run continuously during the campaign and readings must be taken for exactly 4 hours on the first operating shift, and she has not forwarded the monitoring sheet because the laboratory uploaded it after the daily EHS handoff.

acceptance_conditions: The temporary exhaust fan must be authorized.
A dedicated breaker must be required for the fan.
The breaker and interlock installation must be scheduled for exactly 2 hours of downtime.
The fan must run continuously during the solvent-cleaning campaign.
Air monitoring must be scheduled for exactly 4 hours on the first operating shift.
The installation and monitoring actions must be recorded as commitments.
The VOC finding must be cited as justification.

content_checks.C6: decisions['dedicated_breaker_required'] == True and decisions['installation_downtime_hours'] == 2 and any(c['target'] == 'Jon' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: 'continuous' in decisions['fan_run_mode'] and decisions['first_shift_monitoring_hours'] == 4 and any(c['target'] == 'Priya' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The exact dedicated-breaker requirement changes the electrical decision to dedicated_breaker_required=true, while the exact installation duration changes installation_downtime_hours to 2 and requires a maintenance commitment.
The exact 85 ppm reading above the 50 ppm action level changes fan_run_mode to continuous and first_shift_monitoring_hours to exactly 4, with an EHS commitment and cited justification.
